# Ticking reference

The optional tick driver, the tick manager you can call from your own loop, and the interface your own components implement to tick with the simulation. For how to use it, see [Ticking](../modules/ticking.md).

## VtTickDriver

Component. Add it with **Add Component → Vantage → Core → VtTickDriver**.

Scene-placed pump for `VtTickManager`. One `Update` here replaces the per-component `Update` of every registered simulation driver (stats, buffs, abilities, threat, engagement, auras, AI, crafting, resource nodes, spawners, quest logs, projectiles, ground AoE), advancing them in `VtTickGroup` order with one shared `deltaTime`.

### Inspector fields

| Field | Type | Default | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Simulation Time Scale (`simulationTimeScale`) | `float` | 1 | ≥ 0 | Multiplier applied to Time.deltaTime before ticking the simulation. 1 = real time. 0 pauses every registered system without touching Time.timeScale (UI, camera, and combat text keep animating). |

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `bool IsActiveDriver { get; }` | True when this instance is the one pumping the scheduler (a second driver in the scene reports false and does nothing). |

## IVtTickable

Interface. Implemented by [VtAbilityRotation](encounters.md#vtabilityrotation), `VtAbilityScheduler`, [VtAuraEmitter](auras.md#vtauraemitter), `VtBuffScheduler`, [VtBuildSite](building.md#vtbuildsite), [VtCombatEngagement](units.md#vtcombatengagement), [VtCompanionAi](summons.md#vtcompanionai), [VtEncounter](encounters.md#vtencounter), [VtGroundAoeAnchor](abilities.md#vtgroundaoeanchor), [VtHostileAi](ai-roaming.md#vthostileai), [VtMobSpawner](spawning.md#vtmobspawner), [VtPredictedMovementExecutor](movement.md#vtpredictedmovementexecutor), [VtProjectileMover](abilities.md#vtprojectilemover), `VtRegenScheduler`, [VtResourceNode](resource-nodes.md#vtresourcenode), [VtRoaming](ai-roaming.md#vtroaming), [VtSummon](summons.md#vtsummon), [VtThreatTable](threat.md#vtthreattable), [VtUnitAbilities](abilities.md#vtunitabilities), [VtUnitBuffs](units.md#vtunitbuffs), [VtUnitCrafter](crafting.md#vtunitcrafter), [VtUnitOrders](orders.md#vtunitorders), [VtUnitQuestLog](quests.md#vtunitquestlog), [VtUnitRespawn](respawn.md#vtunitrespawn), [VtUnitStats](units.md#vtunitstats), [VtVendor](vendors.md#vtvendor), [VtWorldClock](world-time.md#vtworldclock), `VtWorldClockScheduler`, [VtWorldItem](items.md#vtworlditem).

Something `VtTickManager` advances. Register it with `VtTickManager.Register` in `OnEnable`, unregister it in `OnDisable`, and forward `Update` to `Tick` unless `VtTickManager.IsDriven` is true, so it runs with and without a `VtTickDriver`.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Advance time-based state by `deltaTime` seconds. Called once per step by `VtTickManager`, or from the component's own `Update` when no driver runs. |

## VtTickManager

Static class.

The one registry every simulation component ticks through. With a `VtTickDriver` in the scene, the driver advances every registered component once per frame in `VtTickGroup` order; without one, each component ticks itself from its own `Update`. Servers and replays call `Tick` directly.

### Scripting API

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `static VtTickScheduler Scheduler { get; }` | The live scheduler, for diagnostics such as counting registered components. Use `Register`, `Unregister` and `Tick` for everything else. |
| `static bool IsDriven { get; }` | True while a `VtTickDriver` is enabled and pumping the scheduler. Components read this at the top of `Update` and return early when true so nothing ticks twice. |
| `static void Register(IVtTickable tickable, VtTickGroup group)` | Register a component for central ticking. Safe to call from `OnEnable` regardless of whether a driver exists yet. |
| `static void Unregister(IVtTickable tickable)` | Remove a component. Safe to call from `OnDisable` / `OnDestroy`. |
| `static void Tick(float deltaTime)` | Advance every registered component by `deltaTime` seconds, group by group. `VtTickDriver` calls it once per frame; call it yourself from a server loop or a replay. |

## VtTickGroup

Enum.

The group a tickable runs in. Groups run in the order below, and within a group tickables run in registration order, so state one system produces is visible to the next in the same step.

| Value | Description |
|---|---|
| `Stats` | Runs first: combat timers and resource regeneration. |
| `Auras` | Aura emitters apply and refresh their buffs. |
| `Buffs` | Buff ticks such as damage and healing over time, and expiry. |
| `Abilities` | Cooldowns, cast bars, channels and auto-attacks. |
| `Threat` | Threat decay, after this step's damage has landed. |
| `Movement` | Networked movement: a predicting client's corrections and other clients following the server's position. |
| `Engagement` | Chasing the current target. |
| `Ai` | Roaming and chase decisions of monsters and companions. |
| `World` | World systems: crafting, resource respawn, spawners, quests. Use it for your own world clocks. |
| `Projectiles` | Runs last: projectiles in flight and ground areas. |
